title: 6. Appendix
X's auto-translation turned the world upside down
text:
Reference cases
If you didn't see the frenzy coming, think again.
All it did was turn the 'Show translation' button on by default.
So why did people go wild?
Because fitting into where people already are matters that much.
I'm looking forward to X Chat, due April 17, as well.
All content auto-translated
Launching April 17

title: Cursor changed software by the same principle
text:
Reference cases
AI helped with coding long before Cursor.
But true vibe coding began once Cursor launched,
because it built AI right into the editor.
Before that, you had to jump between an AI chat and your editor.

title: HashChat adds voice rooms so they settle in naturally
text:
Target customer 1
If we offer voice rooms, messaging and similar features well,
users who rely on interpretation have no reason to stay on HelloTalk.
We also expect a viral loop as they invite their partners to HashChat.

title: Multinational meetups
text:
Target customer 2
Tourists and international students in Seoul meet up often.
Most of them don't speak English or Korean well yet.
We give them live interpretation for meeting in person.

title: Meeting locals abroad
text:
Target customer 3
HelloTalk, Reddit and Threads are full of 'let's meet on my trip' posts.
But they usually fizzle out because talking is hard.
Weak matching and no identity checks don't help either.

title: Discord communities of global games
text:
Target customer 4
Global servers are now common, and so is the need to translate.
But Discord has no built-in translation, so people use third-party tools.
Extensions are everywhere, yet they only work on PC.

title: Tourism business owners
text:
Target customer 5
Seoul welcomes huge numbers of tourists every year,
but service workers still aren't ready to talk in other languages.
They need an interpreter that's easy to use.
Taxi drivers
Hotel and guesthouse owners
Restaurant owners
Hair salon owners
Airport desk staff
Cosmetic clinic doctors
Tour guides
And more...
